newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - May 5.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY

- Talks on the restructuring and sale of state-owned resort company Aventura had been temporarily halted while claims on Aventura-owned land were being investigated, industry sources said at the weekend.

- Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko had agreed to hand over power to a transitional authority on the understanding that it would not be immediately headed by rebel leader Laurent Kabila, a senior SA presidential aide said on Sunday.
- Moves to privatise the marketing of government stock have gained momentum, with the finance department asking banks for their views on two key issues - capital requirements and exchange controls.
- Labour's landslide victory in the British elections caused jitters in the financial markets on Friday, with uncertainty over economic policy sparking a sell-off in the pound.
- Ousted ANC KwaZulu-Natal Midlands leader Sifiso Nkabinde would soon join the National Consultative Forum, forum leader Bantu Holomisa said on Sunday.
BUSINESS REPORT

- With only weeks to go before the citrus season ends there is still no sign of export permits being granted to independent parties in terms of the agreement between the government and the Citrus Board, industry sources said on Friday.

- For every 1,000 days the government has been in power, 1,000 previously excluded people have been supplied with fresh, drinkable water under the RDP, Kader Asmal, the minister of water and forestry affairs, said last week.

- Securiplex, a privately owned pet accessories company, is suing Premier Foods for one million rand in damages relating to the alleged non-performance of an alleged verbal agreement that would have resulted in Premier subsidiary Epic Foods buying out Securiplex.

- A member of the Top Dog consortium, a group of minority shareholders in the troubled assurer Crusader Life, denied allegations on Friday that the consortium would receive preferential treatment should the proposed buyout of Crusader by the Hollard insurance group be approved by the high court.

- Rowley Morgan Engineering (RME), the Richards Bay-based firm, has secured a 20 million rand contract to supply 16 barges and eight tugs to the Gotvil Timber group which has been granted a concession to extract hardwoods from the Zaire forests.
SAKE BEELD
- Foreign investors were net buyers of 4.68 billion rand's worth of South African bonds in April this year, bringing total investment to 10.76 billion rand, the South African Bond Exchange said.
THE STAR

- Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has agreed in principle during a meeting with rebel leader Laurent Kabila to relinquish power after more than 30 years, a South African presidential aide said on Sunday.

- National Polic Commissioner George Fivaz and the Police and Prisons Civil Rights Union are headed for a showdown today as the union kicks off industrial action aimed at removing the commissioner from office.

- If visits from local estate agents in your area make you snarl, you are not the only one who wants to bare your teeth at these people. It seems estate agents, like postmen, are universally disliked by the canine population.

- So touched was British BT Challenge yacht skipper James Hatfileld by the personal interest Archbishop Desmond Tutu took in him and his crew of disabled sailors on Sunday, that he described it as being "like a direct line to God".
